cases.query: Can lightning strike the same place twice?
cases.reason: Ordinary recurrence possibility; affirmative declaration includes full supported proposition.

cases.query: Can lightning strike the same object more than once?
cases.reason: Same-object formulation stays within ordinary location/object scope.

cases.query: Lightning never strikes the same place twice. True?
cases.reason: Rejects literal universal never-twice premise; does not copy positive Yes.

cases.query: Is it true that lightning cannot strike the same place twice?
cases.reason: Explicit false-premise declaration rebuts cannot-recur modal.

cases.query: Is the claim that lightning never strikes twice false?
cases.reason: Answers whether never-twice is false declaratively; no inverted short answer.

cases.query: Are tall objects more likely to be struck?
cases.reason: Comparative likelihood is outside existential recurrence.

cases.query: How many times each year is the Empire State Building struck?
cases.reason: Annual counts are excluded.

cases.query: What is the chance lightning will strike this spot again?
cases.reason: Probability at this spot is excluded.

cases.query: Does lightning hit precisely the same microscopic ground coordinates twice?
cases.reason: Microscopic coordinate identity is excluded.

cases.query: How many downward flashes strike the same location?
cases.reason: Direction-specific counts are excluded.

cases.query: Can the same person be struck by lightning twice?
cases.reason: Personal-strike referent is excluded.

cases.query: Do two return strokes count as two independent lightning events?
cases.reason: Event/return-stroke counting definition is excluded.

cases.query: Does lightning always strike the same place twice?
cases.reason: Always is stronger than can; universal recurrence is unsupported.

cases.query: Does lightning strike the same place exactly twice?
cases.reason: Exactly-twice cardinality is unsupported.

cases.query: Does misfortune never happen to someone twice?
cases.reason: Misfortune idiom has a different predicate and referent.

cases.query: Does it strike twice?
cases.reason: Pronoun referent unresolved; clarify.

cases.query: Is it not untrue that lightning cannot never strike twice?
cases.reason: Nested polarity ambiguous; clarify rather than strip negation.

cases.query: Can lightning strike twice, and does that make standing there safe?
cases.reason: Compound safety entailment unsupported; entire C013 answer withheld.

cases.query: Did lightning hit this tower twice yesterday?
cases.reason: Specific historical event not established by generic possibility.

cases.query: Do these sources prove independently replicated recurrence probabilities?
cases.reason: One educational origin does not establish independently replicated probabilities.

cases.query: Can't lightning strike the same place twice?
cases.reason: Negative interrogative answered by capability declaration without Yes/No ambiguity.

cases.query: Lightning never strikes the same place twice, right?
cases.reason: Myth tag question receives explicit false-premise rebuttal.

scope: Manual semantic assessment against frozen accepted predicate and explicit exclusions, not new factual revalidation or general classifier validation.
